title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Oct 3, 2026
summary: The OAS foreign ministers' meeting on Oct. 2 adopted by consensus a resolution demanding free elections, release of political prisoners and disclosure of the disappeared, and created a task force with 60 days to recommend steps. Mexico did not join and Brazil and Uruguay objected to the 'threat to peace' wording; the Dominican Republic said it is closing its embassy in Managua. La Prensa also reported Murillo's Sept. 28 announcement of a free-to-air frequency for Russia's RT. The days-since-'no more elections' KPI advanced to 76.

title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Oct 1, 2026
summary: The OAS extraordinary meeting of foreign ministers on Nicaragua is scheduled for Oct. 2 in Washington; the draft resolution would describe the Ortega-Murillo government as a threat to hemispheric peace and security and ask it to revoke its 2025-2026 reforms and free political prisoners. Nicaragua left the OAS in 2023 and will not take part. No new verified events were found for other sections, so only the days-since-"no more elections" KPI was advanced to 74.

title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Sep 23, 2026
summary: A Sept. 22 UN Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua (GHREN) report found the Ortega-Murillo government responsible for at least eight deaths in state custody since 2018 — including Daniel Ortega's own brother Humberto Ortega, who died in a Managua military hospital in 2024, and Indigenous leader Brooklyn Rivera — and documented 161 enforced disappearances since April 2018, with 29 people still unaccounted for as of Aug. 31. The Colectivo de Derechos Humanos' competing count of 23 disappeared as of the same date is now flagged as a contested figure. The OAS Permanent Council formally set October 2 for an extraordinary foreign ministers' meeting on Nicaragua, following through on its Aug. 19 vote to escalate pressure over Ortega's declared end to elections; Secretary General Ramdin said he expects ministers to go 'beyond symbolism.' Updated the enforced-disappearances KPI to the UN's newer 29 figure, added a KPI tracking the eight documented custody deaths, and added Humberto Ortega to the political figures tracked.

title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Sep 20, 2026
summary: Former OAS Secretary General Luis Almagro said Sept. 19 that an international 'extraction' of Daniel Ortega, comparable to Venezuela's Jan. 3 removal of Nicolás Maduro, would be legally valid and would not violate Nicaraguan sovereignty. The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights escalated a request to the Inter-American Court on Sept. 16 for provisional measures protecting nine political prisoners held since 2014 at La Modelo prison, citing severe conditions and the government's failure to respond. Separately, ICE detained exiled ex-political prisoner Denis Palacios in Virginia on Sept. 16 despite his valid work permit and pending asylum claim, and reporting found six other denationalized exiles from the 2023 group of 222 remain in immigration custody. The US State Department's Sept. 16 drug-transit determination again named Nicaragua's 'illegitimate' government, and co-president Rosario Murillo announced a fifth 2026 mass release of 1,500 common prisoners for Sept. 21 that explicitly excludes the 46+ people still held on political grounds. Updated the days-since-election-ban KPI to 63.

title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 31, 2026
summary: National Assembly President Gustavo Porras confirmed Aug. 29-30 that the Assembly will hold its first vote Sept. 21 on a reform barring denationalized 'traitors to the homeland' from elections, though binding ratification won't come until a legislature convenes after December 2027; Panama recalled its ambassador in protest and Costa Rica, the US and eight other governments plus the OAS and UN voiced concern. An Aug. 30 investigation traced four killings within rights lawyer Thelma Montenegro's family back to 2019, tying her case to a documented pattern of 30+ campesino opposition leaders killed in northern Nicaragua 2018-2019. Marking the UN's Aug. 31 Day of Victims of Enforced Disappearance, a Costa Rica-based rights collective counted 23 Nicaraguans still forcibly disappeared among 60 registered political prisoners, while exiled Bishop Silvio Báez accused the government of 'profaning the name of Jesus' to legitimize its rule. Updated the days-since-election-ban KPI to 43 and added a claim on competing political-prisoner counts.

title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 29, 2026
summary: Human rights lawyer Thelma Montenegro was detained twice within a week — first Aug. 19 at a Pantasma police station while renewing her driver's license, then rearrested Aug. 22 and transferred to Managua without her family being notified until Aug. 25. Eight humanitarian organizations, including CEJIL, demanded her immediate release and proof of life on Aug. 28, with AMA calling it an enforced disappearance. Separately, co-president Rosario Murillo used an Aug. 28 Assembly address backing the pending constitutional reform to brand the Chamorro family 'traitors,' and an Inter-American Dialogue analysis warned the OAS's 29-1 vote for a foreign ministers' session must be followed by concrete measures, noting the session still lacks a confirmed date. Added a new KPI tracking documented enforced disappearances and updated the days-since-election-ban counter to 41.

title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 25, 2026
summary: Nicaragua's Ortega-aligned National Assembly approved a reform on August 24 extending the mandates of 6,320 municipal officials — 153 mayors, 153 vice-mayors, and 6,014 councilmembers — to seven years, canceling the municipal elections that had been scheduled for 2026. The FSLN currently governs all 153 municipalities, and municipal employees and analysts say the reform removes any mechanism for citizens to hold local authorities accountable, extending a pattern that began with 2025's 'Chamuca' reform. The days-since-election-ban KPI was updated to 37, and a new claim captures the government's institutional-continuity framing against critics' accountability concerns.

title: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: Senators Ted Cruz (R-TX) and Tim Kaine (D-VA) introduced a bipartisan bill, the Restoring Electoral Fairness and Opposition Rights through Mandates for Accountability Act, renewing and expanding sanctions on Ortega-Murillo regime officials and newly targeting Nicaragua's gold sector and entities aiding Russia and Iran. The bill builds on Cruz's 2018 NICA Act and conditions sanctions relief on free and fair elections. It follows the OAS's August 19 vote to convene an emergency foreign ministers' session over Ortega's declaration ending elections. Added Sen. Cruz to the political figures tracked and updated the days-since-election-ban KPI to 33.
